max_generations.note: No run hit it (max observed: 140 generations).

early_stop_patience_generations.note: Stops once best_fit_global has stayed the same for patience+1 = 51 consecutive logged generations. Every paper run logged 'Breaking condition reached: No improvement for 50 generations.'

initialization.note: For each individual: aspect ratio uniform from 0.1..2.0; each DSP then each BRAM gets a uniform random (x in [1,width], y in [1,height-h+1]) retrying up to 50 times on column overlap; if any block fails, the whole individual is regenerated. No seeding from the baseline or the policy (log names say 'scratch'). Python random.seed(seed) and np.random.seed(seed) (ga_agent.py:354-356).

genome.value: aspect_ratio gene (one of 20 values 0.1..2.0) + ordered list of DSP (x,y) tile coordinates + ordered list of BRAM (x,y) tile coordinates; one coordinate per H-block the netlist requires

uses_same_legality_masking_as_policy.note: The rules match the policy mask in substance but are separate code: x in [1,width], y in [1,height-h+1], no vertical overlap in the same column (DSP h=4, BRAM h=6). Width/height are the CLI --width/--height (per-run values not logged; logged coordinates stay within the baseline core grid, e.g. arm_core x<=35). Illegal children are repaired, not penalized: crossover collisions get re-sampled positions; a mutation that finds no free spot keeps the old coordinate; if a child has fewer blocks than required it is replaced by a new random individual (ga_agent.py:328-329). Difference from the policy: random coordinates use rejection sampling (up to 50 uniform tries over the bounding box), not the policy's masked categorical over all legal tiles, and an individual with a block that cannot be placed is discarded/regenerated.

selection.value: fitness-proportional roulette wheel, weight = max_processed_fitness - fitness (lower ADP gets more weight); 2 parents drawn independently with replacement per child
selection.note: Failed individuals (fitness inf) are scored 10 x the worst valid fitness for weighting (ga_agent.py:193-199), so the worst individual always has weight 0.

value.type: one-point crossover done separately for the DSP list and the BRAM list (child = A[:cut] + B[cut:], cut uniform in [1,n-1]; lists of length<=1 are copied from parent A); aspect ratio inherited from a uniformly chosen parent; then collision repair

applied to the child with probability 0.7; inside, the aspect ratio gene and each block coordinate are independently resampled with probability 0.7 each (new random legal coordinate; reverts if none found)

mutation.note: The same mut_prob is used both as the per-child chance and as the per-gene chance.

elitism.note: The whole next population is new children, so the best individual is not carried over. The reported result is best_fit_global, the best ever evaluated (ga_agent.py:291-294).

fitness.value: routing_area * critical_path_delay_ns * total_power_w (raw ADP product, no log, no baseline normalization, minimized)
fitness.note: Failed runs (bake returns -1, VTR retcode != 0, or unparseable metrics) get fitness = inf (ga_agent.py:128-129, 142, 154-155, 169-170); for selection they are weighted as 10 x the worst valid fitness. Metrics come from ~/workspace/vtr_exp/run_traditional_flow.py parse_metrics (same VPR report fields as the policy). The GA arch is rendered with ~/workspace/vtr_exp/bake_layout.py using a template byte-identical to vanilla_rl/template/k6_frac_N10_mem32K_40nm.xml.j2, auto_layout with the gene's aspect ratio, and NO VPR atom-pinning constraints file (the policy pins each netlist H-block atom to its coordinate; the GA only places the tiles and lets VPR choose which atom goes where).

vtr_call_counting.value: reported 'GA avg VTR calls' = mean over seeds of (generations logged x 8). There is no cache (every individual in every generation, duplicates included, launches VTR), so cache hits = 0. Failed VTR runs would count as calls; none occurred.

how_set.value: computed as the max fpga_size over the --universe_benchmarks list: compute_max_dims() in src/env/fpga_env.py:95-106 ('max_width = max(res["fpga_size"][0] for res, _, _, _, _ in raw.values())'), called at src/training/trainer.py:73 with universe_names
how_set.note: Universe used for all 3 paper seeds: fifo,ch_intrinsics,spree,boundtop,mmc_core,diffeq1,diffeq2,raygentop,mkSMAdapter4B,or1200,mkPktMerge,softmax,reduction_layer,robot_rl. It includes 2 of the 6 held-out circuits (softmax, reduction_layer) and robot_rl, which is in neither split. It does NOT include custom_macbuf, lightweight_cipher, arm_core, or mkDelayWorker32B. 48x48 (and MAX_NODES/MAX_EDGES) all come from robot_rl (48x48, 67 nodes, 2694 edges); mkDelayWorker32B (48x48) fits exactly. The paper's claim that W_max/H_max are 'taken over both the training pool and the unseen, zero-shot benchmark circuits' is only partly true. baselines/robot_rl_* is now deleted in the working tree (staged), so compute_max_dims can no longer reproduce these dims without restoring it from git.

node_features.note: One node per DSP (instance-id order), then per BRAM, then one fabric node. net_count_normalized = min(unique_nets / 200, 1.0) per block. The fabric node's value is the MEAN net_count_normalized over all non-DSP/BRAM atoms (CLB+IO). No other normalization.

edge_weight.value: sum of shared-net counts between the two reduced nodes (fabric<->fabric dropped, self-pairs dropped), then w_norm = min(log1p(w) / log1p(C), 1), with C = 80 for H-block<->H-block edges and C = 1300 for H-block<->fabric edges; stored symmetrically (both directions)
edge_weight.source: src/netlist/graph_reduction.py:41-42, 150-177; raw edge weight = number of shared nets, src/netlist/analyzer.py:64,119
edge_weight.note: The paper says 'normalized to [0,1]'; the implementation is log-compressed with two different fixed ceilings.

max_edges.note: Directed edge count (each undirected edge stored twice).

zero_net_node_supported.source: src/env/fpga_env.py:70-76 (ValueError if graph DSP/BRAM count != baseline resource requirement), 87-90 (atom-name list dropped if count mismatch); src/netlist/graph_reduction.py:119-123 (nodes only from netlist atoms); src/training/gnn_extractor.py:68 (node validity = is_dsp+is_bram+is_fabric > 0)
zero_net_node_supported.note: The GCN itself would accept it: a node [1,0,0,0] with no edges counts as valid (gnn_extractor.py:68), and GCNConv adds self-loops, so no numerical error. But no code path can create one. Reduced-graph nodes are built only from H-block atoms in the netlist graph JSON, and _load_raw_benchmark raises ValueError if the node counts differ from the VPR resource requirements. The block count to place equals the graph count (fpga_env.py:277). If a spare block were added by hand-editing the JSON + resources file, dsp_block_names/bram_block_names would no longer match the count and would be emptied (fpga_env.py:87-90), which silently drops atom pinning for ALL blocks. The paper's claim is not supported by the current code.

hblock_ordering.value: step 0 = aspect ratio; then all BRAMs, then all DSPs; within each type sorted by net_count_normalized descending (Python sorted, stable, so ties keep instance-id order)
hblock_ordering.note: The paper says 'descending shared-net connectivity'; the implementation sorts by the block's own unique-net count (net_count_normalized), not by shared nets. The VPR pin list is built separately from the .net file, sorted by unique_nets descending (fpga_env.py:83-86), and zipped as dsp_names+bram_names against placed dsps+brams (baker.py:74-85).

value.layer_class: torch_geometric.nn.GCNConv (default normalize=True, add_self_loops=True), edge weights passed as edge_weight
value.readout: global_mean_pool (64) + embedding of current block node (64)

gcn.source: src/training/gnn_extractor.py:41-42, 90-97; printed module in data_export/tools/inspect_model.py output

value.net_arch: SB3 default for MultiInputPolicy: pi=[64,64], vf=[64,64] (separate MLPs)

actor_critic.source: src/training/trainer.py:167-177 (only features_extractor_class passed, no net_arch); module printout from the loaded checkpoint (data_export/tools/inspect_model.py)

total_trainable_parameters.source: data_export/tools/inspect_model.py: sum(p.numel() for p in policy.parameters() if p.requires_grad) on runs/multi11_long_seed42_v2.zip
total_trainable_parameters.note: Features extractor = 37,808 of these (one copy shared by actor and critic; SB3 lists it as pi_ and vf_features_extractor, but they are the same object).

learning_rate.source: checkpoint zip 'data' (lr_schedule ConstantSchedule(val=0.0003)) for all 3 seeds; train.py:29 default; not overridden in wandb-metadata args

n_steps.note: Rollout buffer = 48 x 24 = 1152 steps per update (training log).

total_episodes.note: Stops when >= 13000 episodes are done; the real counts were 13006 / 13003 / 13003 for seeds 7 / 42 / 123 (log 'Reached N episodes', jsonl line counts). The first 13000 go into layouts_multi_seed_*.json.

total_timesteps.note: Training stopped on the episode cap before reaching the timestep target.

formula.value: r = -(1*log(A/A0) + 1*log(D/D0) + 1*log(P/P0) + 0*log(WL/WL0)) = log(ADP0/ADP), with each ratio computed as max(x,1e-9)/max(x0,1e-9); terminal only, 0 at intermediate steps
formula.note: The FPGAEnv constructor defaults (wl .10 pw .30 dl .60 ar 0) are overridden by the trainer. evaluate_held_out.py builds FPGAEnv WITHOUT passing weights (evaluate_held_out.py:68), so the 'reward' field in det_seed*.json uses the constructor defaults, not the training reward. The paper's ADP numbers are computed from raw metrics, so they are unaffected.

failure_penalty.note: Used for an invalid aspect-ratio index, out-of-bounds, overlap (unreachable under masking), bake failure, VTR failure/timeout, or a cached failure. The episode ends.

clipping_or_scaling.note: Only the 1e-9 floor. No reward normalization wrapper (make_vec_env with no VecNormalize, trainer.py:134).

channel_width_mode.value: minimum-channel-width binary search (VPR run 1), then route-only re-run at relaxed W = 1.3 x W_min (VPR run 2; placement reused)
channel_width_mode.source: no --route_chan_width passed (src/evaluation/vtr_runner.py:184-204); vtr_flow/scripts/python_libs/vtr/vpr/vpr.py:19,88-135; e.g. runs/diffeq1_traditional/vpr.out 'successfully routed with a channel width factor of 44' vs vpr_stdout.log '--route_chan_width 58'
channel_width_mode.note: Reported metrics MIX the two runs. routing_area and wirelength come from vpr.out = run 1, the min-W search (vtr_runner.py:120-130). Critical-path delay comes from vpr.crit_path.out and power from <circuit>.power, both written last by run 2 at the relaxed 1.3x W. Check (diffeq1 baseline): metric-file routing_area 694168 = vpr.out (W=44), while vpr_stdout.log (W=58) reports 904549; delay 22.3395 = relaxed-run value (vpr.out min-W run: 22.503).

area_metric.value: VPR 'Total routing area' in minimum-width transistor areas (MWTA), from the min-W search run
area_metric.note: Routing area only; logic block area is not included.

delay_metric.value: 'Final critical path delay (least slack)' in ns from vpr.crit_path.out (relaxed-W run)

power_metric.value: first 'Total' row (column 2) of <circuit>.power, in W (VPR power estimation, --power --tech_properties 45nm.xml)
power_metric.note: This is total power (dynamic + leakage) as reported by VPR's power model. Activity: VTR flow default ACE2 run (runs/*/ace.out: 'ace -b ... -c clk -n ... -o <c>.act -s 1', 'Input activities will be assumed (0.500000, 0.200000, 0.200000)'), ace_seed=1 (python_libs/vtr/ace/ace.py:19). No user activity file.

technology_file.note: The arch is the '40nm' k6_frac_N10_mem32K file; power uses the 45nm PTM tech properties.

vpr_placer_seed.note: Fixed VPR default. The GA uses the same default.

vtr_parallelism.value: policy training: up to 24 concurrent VTR flows (one per SubprocVecEnv worker, --n_envs 24); zero-shot eval: 1 at a time; GA: 8 concurrent (ThreadPoolExecutor over the population)
vtr_parallelism.note: The per-episode VTR timeout during training was 300 s (--vtr_timeout 300), 1200 s in eval. Timeouts count as failures (-10).

construction.value: auto_layout aspect_ratio=1.0: io perimeter, EMPTY corners, clb fill; mult_36 (DSP, 4 rows tall) columns at startx=6 repeatx=8 starty=1; memory (BRAM, 6 rows tall) columns at startx=2 repeatx=8 starty=1; EMPTY where a block does not fit; grid auto-sized by VPR to the smallest square that holds the netlist

provisioning_margin.note: e.g. diffeq1: needs dsp 5 / bram 0, provides dsp 6 / bram 4. Per-circuit numbers are in the resources files.

key.value: string f"dsps:{list(placed_dsps)}|brams:{list(placed_brams)}|ratio:{aspect_ratio}" in a per-benchmark SQLite DB runs/vtr_layout_cache_{benchmark}{cache_suffix}.db
key.note: Order-sensitive (the j-th coordinate is pinned to the j-th atom). Architecture/template/VTR version/timeout are not in the key. The DB is shared by every run on that benchmark with the same cache_suffix: all 3 paper seeds, the older seed-42 v1 run, and the 13-benchmark runs all used '' on shared circuits, so later runs got hits from earlier runs (seed 7's first logged new-best was already 'Cached : True'). Failures are cached too, including timeouts, so a timeout under load is permanently a failure for that key.

heldout_circuits.note: The paper labels custom_macbuf as 'macbuf' and lightweight_cipher as 'cipher'.

how_split_chosen.value: The 11 training circuits were the 'light-tier' benchmarks; 'heavy-tier' circuits (softmax, reduction_layer, robot_rl) were held out, later extended with arm_core, the two authored probes, and mkDelayWorker32B. The final held-out set of 6 was a decision pending advisor sign-off, weighing whether to include the volatile mkDelayWorker32B.
how_split_chosen.note: No stated statistical or random split procedure. robot_rl was dropped ('timeout issue, canvas sizing bug', PAPER_PLAN.md:174) but stayed in the sizing universe.

value.custom_macbuf: hand-written 3-tap weighted multiply-accumulate pipeline: reads an input sample buffer, three independent 32-bit multiplies, writes accumulated results to an output buffer (netlist: 3 DSP, 1 BRAM)
value.lightweight_cipher: hand-written byte-serial SPN block cipher core: 8-bit S-box lookup per clock, wire-level byte rotation, key XOR with LFSR-style round-key update (netlist: 0 DSP, 3 BRAM)

authored_probes.note: custom_macbuf's header says '(3 DSP, 2 BRAM)', but VPR infers 1 BRAM (baselines/custom_macbuf_traditional_resources.txt).

aspect_ratios.note: Passed as the VTR auto_layout aspect_ratio attribute (width/height).
